Chapter 1. Affine Schemes

1.1. The Spectrum of a Ring

In this chapter we develop the foundations of affine schemes. The central construction associates to a commutative ring its prime spectrum, a topological space equipped with a structure sheaf. We assume familiarity with basic commutative algebra throughout this exposition.

Theorem 1.1 (Spec Functoriality).

For every ring homomorphism φ:A→B the induced map on spectra is continuous.

Proof.

The preimage of a basic open set D(f) under the induced map is the basic open set D(φ(f)). Since basic open sets form a basis for the Zariski topology, continuity follows.

Chapter 2. Sheaves of Modules

2.1. Quasi-coherent Sheaves

A quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme corresponds to a module over the underlying ring. This equivalence of categories is the cornerstone of the theory and allows algebraic computations to be reinterpreted geometrically.

Lemma 2.1 (Module-Sheaf Equivalence).

The global-sections functor and the tilde construction are mutually inverse equivalences between modules and quasi-coherent sheaves.

Proof.

One checks the unit and counit of the adjunction are isomorphisms on the basis of distinguished open sets, then extends by the sheaf condition.
